localChanges: chore: lock the engine packages that give leaders their personalities

log: Generic rule types for what a leader's personality makes a computer player do (AdvanceGrade, AttackConfidence, BuildWeight, Expansion, MilitaryUnhappinessTolerance, ScienceBias, WantedAdvances), a leaderHas criterion, and sum, product and union for how the rules for a leader's several traits combine (civ-clone/web-renderer#157).
chore: build with pnpm on the standard workflow, and check formatting

Registers Civ1's values for the base-leader-personality rules, from where v474.05's AI reads Mood, Policy and Ideology: science bias and military unhappiness tolerance by Ideology, the advances each leader wants before it stops researching (moved from simple-ai-client), Settlers kept by Policy and Ideology, improvements weighed by Ideology, the research grade table (F0_1ade_2317, DS:0x0b0a) and attack confidence by Mood (civ-clone/web-renderer#157).
chore: rebuild a source map that was compiled before formatting
Importing personalityRules or register no longer adds rules to defaultGame; index.ts registers them after the traits. Also rewords two comments, as Copilot suggested.

Trade rates read ScienceBias, the Republic score reads MilitaryUnhappinessTolerance, and the advances a leader wants before science stops come from WantedAdvances rules, which civ1-civilization registers with the same values. lib/traits and the Civ1 wanted-advances table go. Play is unchanged: web-renderer's conformance checksums match (civ-clone/web-renderer#157).
chore: drop the leader trait packages, which nothing imports now

Expansion scales the Settlers a player keeps, BuildWeight weighs the random pick of what a city builds, AdvanceGrade grades research as v474.05 does (each available advance draws below 4 x its grade, the highest wins), and AttackConfidence scales a player's strength in shouldAttack, which negotiation also asks. With no such rules, play is as before (civ-clone/web-renderer#157).
chore: rebuild a source map that was compiled before formatting

A ruleset's AdvanceGrade rules for one leader's trait no longer turn every other leader's research into always taking the first advance available: with no rule matching the player and any of its choices, it picks at random with one draw, as before.

civ1DisorderPolicy.unhappinessOnGrowth still had Civ1's old five content citizens for everyone. Since difficulty levels (civ-clone/web-renderer#173) a computer player's cities are born with three, on every level, so the AI didn't see its cities of 3 to 5 growing into disorder. The PreventDisorder tests size their cities for three content citizens.
test: size the martial law and trade-rate cities for a computer player's three content citizens
